source_observations: BudgetGuard separates pre-call check from post-call record and fail-closes budget violations.
It supports max calls, token caps, optional USD caps, per-task/global kill switch and sliding-window repeated-signature rejection.

Loop detection counts identical supplied signatures; the upstream security document explicitly warns that perturbed or interleaved loops can evade raw signatures and recommends semantic normalization.
The ledger and kill switches are in-memory and do not survive process restart or span processes/machines.
The upstream security document identifies check-then-act concurrency as a known overshoot race until a future reserve/commit API exists.

The inspected tests and property-test source exercise cap enforcement, repeated-signature rejection and fail-closed malformed-token handling; this run did not execute upstream tests, so no runtime/reproduction credit is granted.

initial_f2_relevance.reason: Current F2 WP509 already has bounded iteration, unchanged-state, remaining-work and typed-exit semantics. BudgetGuard may still provide an independent adversarial lens on repetition signatures and pre-call admission, but importing its in-memory ledger would duplicate authority and weaken restart/causal boundaries.

counterhypotheses: A semantic action signature may catch loop classes that F2 unchanged-state counters miss.
Conversely, signature repetition may falsely stop valid repeated actions that produce changing evidence; result/progress identity must be separated from action identity before adoption.
